title: Indonesian Tamarind Pork Satay Batches
seoTitle: Indonesian Tamarind Pork Satay Batches | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Satay skewer night—tamarind-turmeric marinade, kecap manis lacquer, warm peanut sauce
subtitle: Coconut-marinated pork skewers, peanut sauce, and cucumber pickle for the crew
description: Pork shoulder strips in a blended lemongrass-galangal-tamarind marinade, grilled hot on skewers, lacquered with a kecap manis peanut baste, and served over jasmine rice with a sharp cucumber pickle.

steps.title: Toast and grind the coriander
steps.instruction: Toast the coriander seeds in a dry skillet over medium heat, shaking constantly, 60–90 seconds until they smell nutty and start to pop. Scorched coriander turns acrid, so pull them the moment they're fragrant. Grind fine in a spice grinder or crush under the bottom of a heavy pan.

steps.title: Blend the satay marinade
steps.instruction: Blend the minced lemongrass cores, grated galangal, ground coriander, turmeric, tamarind paste, brown sugar, fish sauce, and half the coconut cream into a smooth, mustard-yellow paste, about 1 minute. This is the classic Indonesian base — sour tamarind pushing against the sugar, with turmeric doing the color. If it won't turn over in the blender, add coconut cream a spoonful at a time.

steps.title: Slice and marinate the pork
steps.instruction: Slice the pork shoulder against the grain into strips about 1/4 inch thick, 1 inch wide, and 3–4 inches long — shoulder's marbling keeps skewers juicy where lean loin dries out. Toss the strips with the marinade and refrigerate at least 2 hours, overnight if you're working ahead; the turmeric and tamarind need time to travel past the surface.

steps.title: Soak skewers, pickle the cucumbers
steps.instruction: Drop the bamboo skewers in water for 30 minutes so they don't torch over the fire. Slice the English cucumbers into thin coins and toss with the rice vinegar, a spoonful of sugar, and a pinch of salt; chill until service. The sharp pickle is not optional — it resets your palate between rich, sweet skewers.

steps.title: Warm the peanut sauce, split it in two
steps.instruction: Warm the creamy peanut butter, kecap manis, remaining coconut cream, a spoonful of tamarind paste, and the sambal oelek in a saucepan over low heat, whisking 3–4 minutes until it pours like heavy cream — loosen with warm water if it seizes into paste. Split it into two bowls: one for basting at the grill, one clean for the table. The basting bowl touches raw meat and never leaves the cook's station.

steps.title: Thread the skewers flat
steps.instruction: Thread the pork ribbon-style onto the soaked skewers, keeping each strip flat and snug with the sharp tip covered. Pat off the excess marinade with paper towels — a wet, dripping skewer flares up and steams instead of charring. Get the steamed jasmine rice going now so it lands hot with the first batch.

steps.title: Grill hot and fast, in batches
steps.instruction: Grill the skewers over medium-high, 425–450°F, about 3 minutes per side, until the edges char and the marinade caramelizes. Thin strips move fast — probe the thickest skewer with an instant-read and pull the batch at 145°F. Crowding the grates drops the fire and the pork stews gray instead of charring, so leave a finger's width between skewers.

steps.title: Lacquer with the basting bowl
steps.instruction: Brush the skewers with the basting bowl of peanut sauce and give them 45–60 seconds per side more over the fire until the glaze goes sticky and deep brown at the edges. The kecap manis is loaded with sugar — past 450°F or 90 seconds it jumps from lacquer to carbon, so watch the color, not the clock.

steps.title: Rest, then platter over rice
steps.instruction: Rest the skewers 3 minutes so the juices settle, then platter over the steamed jasmine rice with the cucumber pickle alongside and torn Thai basil scattered over everything. Set out the clean bowl of warm peanut sauce for spooning — start each firefighter with two skewers and a ladle of sauce.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover pork satay skewers — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool pork satay and hot components in shallow hotel pans within two hours — deep pots stay in the danger zone too long. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Marinate overnight when you can — the turmeric and tamarind keep working, and day-of prep drops to threading skewers.
Two sauce bowls, always: baste from one, serve from the other. The basting bowl never goes to the table.
If the peanut sauce seizes into paste, whisk in warm water a tablespoon at a time — it loosens back to pourable.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Log hold times on the pan with a grease pencil when tones drop mid-service.
Spot-check proteins with an instant-read thermometer before reopening the line after a call.
tonightSpread: Main: Tamarind pork satay skewers with warm peanut sauce
Sides: steamed jasmine rice, cucumber pickle
Condiments: sambal oelek, extra peanut sauce
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool pork satay in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
Strip day-two satay off the skewers into fried rice or lettuce cups with the leftover peanut sauce.
Peanut sauce keeps 4 days chilled; loosen with warm water when you rewarm it.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Charred skewers with a sticky kecap manis lacquer and a peanut sauce worth arguing over — handheld, fast off the fire, and nothing like another pulled pork night.
mealPrepNotes: Marinate the pork 2–24 hours. Cook skewers at 425–450°F to 145°F, glaze in the last minute, and hold covered at 140°F or above up to 30 minutes. Keep the table's peanut sauce warm on the lowest burner.
substitutions: Chicken thighs swap 1:1 for the pork — same slicing, but cook the skewers to 165°F instead.
No galangal? Fresh ginger works — sharper and less piney, so use a touch less.
Out of kecap manis: simmer 3 parts soy sauce with 2 parts brown sugar until syrupy.
No tamarind paste? Lime juice plus an extra spoon of brown sugar fakes the sweet-sour angle.
